I've conducted an exhaustive investigation into why MCPs cannot be effectively disabled in OpenCode, and I believe your issue (#13763) touches on a symptom of a deeper architectural problem that may not be fully solved by simply persisting toggle state.

**Key finding**: at least two MCPs — `chrome-devtools` and `morphllm-fast-apply` — are **hardcoded into the `opencode` binary** itself. They spawn automatically on every startup (visible in logs as `service=mcp key=chrome-devtools type=local found`) even when the user's `opencode.json` contains no reference to them.

This means:
- Persisting `/mcps` toggle state will help **user-defined** MCPs, but it will **not** give users a way to turn off these binary-bundled defaults.
- Attempting to add `"chrome-devtools": { "enabled": false }` to `opencode.json` currently produces a fatal schema validation error (`Invalid input mcp.chrome-devtools`) in the session attach path.
- The public JSON schema (`https://opencode.ai/config.json`) does not even declare an `mcp` property; validation is handled by an internal zod schema that rejects built-in names.

I've opened a dedicated feature request (#22188) specifically requesting an official mechanism to disable built-in MCP servers. It may be worth considering that fix alongside toggle persistence so that users can actually opt out of **all** MCPs, not just the ones they manually configured.

Evidence summary: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/22188

I ran into the same fundamental problem from the end-user / TUI side and did a deep-dive into the root causes. One significant finding: `chrome-devtools` and `morphllm-fast-apply` are **spawned by the `opencode` binary itself** rather than from user configuration, so even isolating `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` into an empty `opencode.json` (`{"mcp":{}}`) does not prevent these built-in MCPs from loading when running the full TUI or desktop app.

This means the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` workaround you documented works for **SDK callers**, but end users still have no supported way to start a lean OpenCode session with zero MCP overhead.

I've submitted a feature request (#22188) asking for an official kill switch (e.g. `disabled_mcp_servers` array or respecting `enabled: false` for built-ins). It references your workaround as the current best option for the SDK path, but highlights that a broader fix is needed for the binary-bundled defaults.

Adding a "Disable ALL" toggle would help, but our investigation found that it may still leave **binary-bundled MCPs** active. Specifically:

- `chrome-devtools` and `morphllm-fast-apply` are spawned automatically by the `opencode` binary on every session startup.
- They load even when `opencode.json` has an empty `"mcp": {}` section.
- There is currently no schema-supported way to disable them via configuration.

If a global "Disable ALL" feature is implemented, it would ideally need to intercept and suppress these built-in defaults as well as user-defined ones. I've opened #22188 to track the built-in MCP disable request specifically; linking it here in case the two features should be designed together.

Project-level MCP isolation would be a huge improvement, but a detail that might affect the design: some MCPs are **not inherited from global config at all** — they are launched directly by the `opencode` binary.

Our logs show `chrome-devtools` and `morphllm-fast-apply` loading as `type=local found` even when the global `opencode.json` contains no such entries (`"mcp": {}`). This means project-level opt-out would need to be able to override **binary defaults**, not just inherited global servers.

I've filed #22188 specifically to request a built-in MCP disable mechanism. It might be worth aligning that work with this project-isolation feature so that the final design can suppress both inherited global MCPs and hardcoded binary-bundled ones.

## Additional reproduction — real session bricked (April 12, 2026)

Hit this bug again in a live session on WSL2/Ubuntu 24.04 (OpenCode on `dev`, Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6).

### Sequence that triggered it

1. Session running normally — `sdd-init`, then web research via `webfetch`, then checking WSLg via parallel `bash` calls
2. Assistant made a `todowrite` call (internal tool, **not MCP**) → completed successfully
3. Assistant generated text after the tool result
4. Step finished with `"finish": "tool-calls"` — model wanted to continue
5. Next API call → **400: `tool_use` ids found without `tool_result` blocks**
6. Session permanently bricked

### Key evidence from the SQLite session dump

**Orphaned tool call**: `toolu_01U3gvtjXYHzq121oQG6624z` (a `todowrite`)

The part data shows `"status":"completed"` with valid output — the tool executed fine. But when the message history was serialized for the next API request, the `tool_result` was not placed in the required `user` message after the `assistant` message containing the `tool_use`.

**Error response** (from `msg_d832e2af7001`):
```
messages.17: `tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result` blocks
immediately after: toolu_01U3gvtjXYHzq121oQG6624z
```

### Why this rules out network/MCP

- DNS was verified working (immutable `/etc/resolv.conf` with Cloudflare) — repo was cloned successfully right before this session
- The failing tool is `todowrite` — an **internal OpenCode tool**, not an MCP server tool
- All previous tool calls in the same session completed normally

### Why `ensureToolIntegrity()` would have caught this

The fix in this PR scans for orphaned `tool_use` blocks and injects synthetic `tool_result` messages. This exact scenario — a completed `todowrite` whose result was lost during serialization — would have been patched before the API call.

Different operating systems - different problems

**Code-level fix proposals based on source analysis:**

**1. `src/util/queue.ts` — Add capacity limit**

Currently `AsyncQueue` has no size limit. Items pushed are never dropped:
```typescript
// queue.ts:5-9 — unbounded
push(item: T) {
  const resolve = this.resolvers.shift()
  if (resolve) resolve(item)
  else this.queue.push(item)  // ← no limit
}
```
Proposed: add constructor parameter `limit` (default 10000). When queue exceeds limit, either drop oldest items or return `false` to signal overflow so the caller (SSE handler) can close the connection.

**2. `src/server/instance/event.ts:46-53` — Add idle timeout**

Currently heartbeat pushes every 10s forever, even if the consumer (SSE client) is dead:
```typescript
const heartbeat = setInterval(() => {
  q.push(JSON.stringify({ type: "server.heartbeat", properties: {} }))
}, 10_000)
```
Proposed: track `lastConsumed` timestamp. If nothing was consumed for 60s, call `stop()`. Update `lastConsumed` after each successful `stream.writeSSE()`.

**3. `src/server/instance/event.ts:71` — Don't rely solely on `onAbort`**

Currently cleanup ONLY runs via `stream.onAbort(stop)` — which never fires when the TCP socket enters CLOSE_WAIT in Bun/Hono:
```typescript
stream.onAbort(stop)  // ← never called on TCP half-close
```
Proposed: wrap `stream.writeSSE()` in try/catch. A write error means the socket is dead — trigger `stop()` immediately. This covers the CLOSE_WAIT case regardless of whether `onAbort` fires.

**4. `src/lsp/client.ts:52` — Prune diagnostics for closed files**

Currently `diagnostics = new Map<string, Diagnostic[]>()` grows unbounded. Entries are only replaced on file re-open (`diagnostics.delete(input.path)` at line 194, then re-add). Files that are closed and never re-opened stay forever. For TypeScript language server reporting diagnostics on 1000+ files, this accumulates significantly over time.

**5. `src/mcp/index.ts` — Kill previous MCP processes before spawning new ones**

Observed 7-10× duplicate MCP process sets (docker, mcp-lsp-bridge, playwright). The `closeClient()` function at line 548 exists but is apparently not called when instances are re-initialized. Instance disposal should properly close all MCP clients before new ones are created.

**Windows Desktop memory leak — SSE CLOSE_WAIT + MCP process duplication (v1.4.3)**

Environment: Windows 11 x64, OpenCode Desktop 1.4.3, Bun runtime, single user session.

**Evidence of SSE CLOSE_WAIT zombie connections:**

`opencode-cli.exe` memory grows up to **24.5 GB**. The growth correlates with TCP connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT state on the server port:

```
T+0min:  RAM 0.96 GB | Alive 12 | Zombie 66
T+30min: RAM 2.5 GB  | Alive 12 | Zombie 66
T+60min: RAM 3.69 GB | Alive 6  | Zombie 70
Peak:    RAM 24.5 GB | Alive 2  | Zombie 74
```

Growth rate measured at **+434 MB in 30 seconds (14.5 MB/sec)** with stable zombie count — existing zombie queues fill up continuously.

Each SSE connection creates an unbounded `AsyncQueue` (`src/util/queue.ts`) that receives ALL Bus events + heartbeats every 10s. When the TCP connection enters CLOSE_WAIT, `stream.onAbort(stop)` (the only cleanup path in `src/server/instance/event.ts:71`) never fires in Bun/Hono, so:
- `clearInterval(heartbeat)` never runs → heartbeat keeps pushing every 10s
- `Bus.subscribeAll()` unsubscribe never runs → all events keep flowing
- `AsyncQueue` grows without bound

Same pattern in `src/server/instance/global.ts` `streamEvents()` for `/global/event` and `/global/sync-event`.

**MCP process duplication:**

7× docker.exe, 10× mcp-lsp-bridge.exe, 7× cmd.exe (playwright), 1× mcp-server-qdrant.exe — should be 1 set per project, not 7-10.

**Note on `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT`:** As @sjawhar documented, `process.memoryUsage().rss` drastically underreports in Bun (358MB reported vs 22GB real). On my process at 3.94 GB actual RSS, the auto-snapshot threshold (2GB based on `process.memoryUsage()`) may never trigger. This needs the `/proc/self/statm` workaround (Linux) or equivalent on Windows.
